text:
Sam R: Heads up — saw ~30 ALB targets get deregistered from edge pool us-east-2 between 15:03–15:06. Targets show Unhealthy before removal. Not obvious app crash. Anyone seen similar today?

Maya P: seeing same in metrics. Healthcheck 502/504s, lots of retries. NLB/ALB logs show HTTP 504 from probe -> backend timed out.

Devon L: grabbing pod logs now. Quick check: readyProbe failures spike right after autoscaler adds nodes. Could be cold-start readiness jitter.

Kyle T: are these GPU nodes with slow startup (nv driver + container init)? That can push readinessProbe timeouts.

Sam R: yes, these are edge-inference pools (g4dn-like). startup logs show model mmap + warmup ~8s. readinessProbe is http GET /ready  with timeoutSeconds: 1 and failureThreshold: 3.

Maya P: that timeoutSeconds:1 is brutal during cold start. But ALB health checks come every 10s with unhealthy threshold 2 -> deregister quickly.

Devon L: pasted recent ALB access log snippet: 
```
2026-03-17T15:03:21Z target:10.0.12.45 status:504 elb_status:504 target_status:504
2026-03-17T15:03:31Z target:10.0.12.45 status:200 elb_status:200 target_status:200
```
Suggests ephemeral probe failures, then recovery.

Kyle T: could also be SNAT port churn if many pods start simultaneously and egress to model registry TTL causes transient routing. Check node conntrack/snat metrics.

Maya P: node conntrack peaks exactly at the time of scale-up: conntrack entries jumped to 120k (+50k). SNAT port avail drops to single digits on some nodes.

Sam R: oh nice catch. So two overlapping effects: cold readiness + SNAT pressure causing probe packets to be dropped or delayed -> ALB sees timeouts -> deregisters target.

Devon L: short-term mitigation: increase readinessProbe timeoutSeconds to 5 and failureThreshold to 5 for edge pool. Also add a 30s startup pause before registering with service.

Kyle T: +1. For the ALB side we can increase unhealthy threshold to 5 or healthcheck interval to 15s to reduce sensitivity to jitter. But that's a bit global for edge pool only.

Maya P: running quick experiment: patching deployment to set readinessProbe.timeoutSeconds=5 and failureThreshold=5 for one canary. Also enabling hostNetwork=false -> reduces SNAT per pod? (ops: hostNetwork false is current state).

Sam R: can we also add a postStart sleep: 10s in container lifecycle to let drivers initialize? e.g., 
```yaml
lifecycle:
  postStart:
    exec: {"command":["/bin/sh","-c","sleep 10"]}
```

Devon L: will apply canary now to pool-edge-inference-1. Patch and watch.

sre-bot: Incident INC-2026 created (lb-health-flap-edge). Pager notified. :rotating_light:

(10s later)

Devon L: canary patched. Observing healthchecks — failures dropped from ~20/min to ~2/min. ALB didn't deregister the canary target.

Maya P: conntrack still spiky but less impact on the patched pod. We should reduce ephemeral egress during boot (avoid external registries in init).

Sam R: action items:
- Devon: roll readiness probe change to all edge pools (patch + rollout)
- Kyle: propose ALB healthcheck relax policy for edge target group (interval 15s, unhealthy threshold 4)
- Maya: add conntrack alerting threshold and investigate SNAT autoscaling options (egress NAT gateway, ip-per-pod CNI, or keepalive proxies)
- Ops: add small postStart sleep and avoid external egress during model mmap if possible

Kyle T: I'll draft ALB change and a scoped rollout to avoid global risk.

Devon L: rolling out readiness change now, will monitor for 30m.

Sam R: thanks everyone. We'll keep this thread updated. If ALB still evicts after rollout, we'll open a follow-up and escalate to networking. :thumbsup:
